memberdef.name: XtcCompileTask

detaileddescription.para: This goes through the Gradle build script, and task creation through the project ObjectFactory.

The reason we need the @Inject is that the Kotlin compiler adds a secret parameter to the generated constructor, if the class uses variables from the build script. That parameter is a reference to the enclosing build script. As a result, the task needs to have the @Inject annotation in the constructor so that Gradle will correctly instantiate the task with build script reference (which is what happens when you instantiate it from the ObjectFactory in a project):

briefdescription.para: Override to return source-set-specific dependencies for compilation.

detaileddescription.para: This avoids the circular dependency where a compile task's own output appears in its inputs (via xtcModuleDependencies from all source sets).
Main compile: only external dependencies from xtcModule Test compile: xtcModule + xtcModuleTest (includes main output)

briefdescription.para: Returns all XTC source files (including subdirectory files) for incremental build tracking.

detaileddescription.para: This ensures Gradle detects changes in subdirectory .x files that are part of the module compilation unit, even though only top-level module files are passed to the XTC compiler.
This method fixes the incremental build issue where changes to subdirectory .x files (like xenia/BundlePool.x) were not triggering recompilation of the parent module.

briefdescription.para: Rename all valid XTC modules in the compile output to their final names, if such names are specified in the DSL for the compile task (the outputFilenames property with its value pairs).
